independence_declaration.statement:
domain-reviewer authored no DG2 implementation, test, register row or ADR in the reviewed candidate. I formed this verdict from my own runs in a disposable clone at 5699f721 (the freeze commit on source aa0a68f1). I did not open any other reviewer's round-13 record. The only earlier material I reused was my own domain-review tooling from rounds 4-12:
- with-stack.sh: only the ports and clone path changed, plus it now exports API_PID/API_LOG.
- walk-ui.mjs: only the screenshot names changed.
New in round 13: source-fidelity.mjs, r13-delta-api.mjs, r13-ui.mjs, r13-ui-withdrawn.mjs, r13-shutdown.mjs, r13-session-end-ui.mjs and with-stack-default-limits.sh. I read the implementers' commit-time-auth integration test only to learn the API shapes for withdrawing access.

Sequencing, the charter and its thesis, the scope checks, the North Star, outcomes, guardrails, the TOM and the invisible-only refusals are checked along the way.
checks_run.command: bash with-stack.sh bash rv/api-runs.sh -> node rv/live-scenario.mjs (stack-run-1-attempt1.log)
checks_run.environment: disposable PostgreSQL 16 :55023 (UTF8) + API AUTH_MODE=dev :3923; SYNTHETIC seed; Node 24.21.0
checks_run.expected: G2/G3 before G1 refused 422 gate.out_of_sequence; G1, G2 and G3 approved in order with the phase advancing diagnose->define->design->mobilize; all source rules hold
checks_run.actual:
101/101 PASS, exit 0.
- Sequencing: G2/G3 before G1 gave 422 gate.out_of_sequence, and G3 before G2 gave 422.
- G1 lists its 6 outputs; the submitter cannot decide (403); G1 is approved (diagnose->define).
- G2 is blocked at zero guardrails (422 naming g2.guardrails); G2 is approved (define->design).
- G3 is blocked while the gap matrix, capability gaps and journeys are missing; G3 is approved (design->mobilize).
- Gate names equal B0023; exactly one current North Star; thesis incomplete when a part is blank or invisible-only; the five B0039-43 checks are in source order; the 3-5 top-outcome warning shows; 'Launch new app' fails the good-outcome test.
- 10 TOM dimensions with B0056 questions, 6 workstreams with B0029 questions, 10 canvas boxes with B0062 prompts.
- Invisible-only values give 400 validation.blank, and Arabic text with RLM is stored verbatim.
- The value pool shows 'unquantified' with amount null (not 0).
- Only gate codes G1-G6 exist.
The G1-G3 decisions are synthetic demo decisions and approve nothing real.

checks_run.command: node rv/r13-delta-api.mjs (attempt 1 in stack-run-1-attempt1.log; attempt 2 in stack-run-1b-attempt2.log; attempt 3 in stack-run-1b.log)
checks_run.environment: fresh disposable stack per attempt; SYNTHETIC; Node 24.21.0
checks_run.expected: normal uploads 200 and byte-identical; withdrawn access 403 forbidden (audited) or 401 unauthenticated; nothing stored; no .part left; later uploads work; dev sign-in works
checks_run.actual:
Attempt 3: 11/11 PASS, exit 0.
- EN and AR uploads (2 MiB): 200, byte-identical, file names kept.
- Access reaching its effectiveTo mid-stream: 403 forbidden, one authorization.denied audit (transformation, content route), 0 revisions, version unchanged, a .part present during the stream and none afterwards.
- After revoking the expired assignment and re-granting, dev.nobody's upload is 200 and byte-identical.
- Admin revoke mid-stream: 401 unauthenticated, /me 401, nothing stored, no .part.
- Sign-out mid-stream: 401, nothing stored; the lead's other session still uploads (200).
- 'forbidden' and 'unauthenticated' are localized EN and AR.
- dev-login gives 204 and /me 200 for all five seeded users.
- GET /auth/login is 404 in dev mode (the OIDC path is residual D-049).
Attempts 1 and 2 exited 1 because of MY probe errors, not product errors:
- (1) I counted denials by the evidence id; the audit records the transformation.
- (1) I expected the lead to upload to dev.nobody's item; the ownership rule rightly gives 403.
- (2) Re-granting while the expired, unrevoked assignment existed gave 409 (a uniqueness rule), and my probe then crashed on an undefined id.

checks_run.procedure: SIGTERM the API while an upload body is still arriving. Check that no partial file or revision remains and that the final objects are unchanged. Restart the API and confirm that evidence upload and download work.
checks_run.command: node rv/r13-shutdown.mjs (attempt 1 in stack-run-3-attempt1.log; attempt 2 in stack-run-3.log)
checks_run.environment: fresh disposable stack; the probe stops the stack's idle API and runs its own API child with LOG_LEVEL=info; SYNTHETIC
checks_run.expected: exit code 0 within the 10 s backstop; 'shut down' logged with no settle warning; 0 .part files; 0 revisions for the cut item; after a restart, the earlier file is byte-identical and a new upload works
checks_run.actual:
Attempt 2: 2/2 PASS, exit 0.
- One .part existed during the stream. The API logged 'shutting down SIGTERM', 'shutdown grace period elapsed', 'request body not received completely' and 'shut down SIGTERM', and exited with code 0 after 5030 ms, with no settle warning.
- Afterwards: 0 .part files, 0 revisions for the cut item, final objects unchanged (1->1). The client's connection was closed.
- After the restart, the start-up sweep logged removed 0 (olderThanMs 3600000); the earlier file downloads byte-identical, and the cut item takes a 200 upload that downloads byte-identical. The restarted API exited with code 0.
Attempt 1 exited 1 because of MY probe error: with-stack.sh runs the API at LOG_LEVEL=warn, so the info line 'shut down' is never written. Its other assertions (no .part, 0 revisions, exit within 5.1 s) already held.

checks_run.command: node rv/r13-ui.mjs (stack-run-2.log); rv/r13-ui-withdrawn.mjs (stack-run-3-attempt1.log, stack-run-3.log); rv/r13-session-end-ui.mjs (stack-run-4.log; stack-run-5.log via with-stack-default-limits.sh)
checks_run.environment: fresh disposable stacks; Chromium; SYNTHETIC; stacks 2-4 with raised rate limits, stack 5 with defaults
checks_run.expected: after the 401 the user lands once on the sign-in page with the localized session-ended message and the form (ltr/rtl), with a bounded number of /me requests; signing in again works
checks_run.actual:
FAIL (F-DG2-480, High). The server answers correctly: upload 401, 0 revisions. The client then:
- shows the dialog's localized message for about 5 ms, then a blank page that alternates between /login?…error=session_expired and the page for at least 15 s;
- never shows the sign-in form or the message;
- sends 1411 (EN) and 1265 (AR) /me requests in 10 s.
The same loop follows a sign-out in another tab plus an in-app link, with no upload involved. A reload recovers in about 0.4 s (control PASS).
With default limits (300/min), the IP bucket is exhausted after about 283 /me calls. The tab then shows a stale signed-in shell with 'Too many requests', and the next browser context from the same IP could not get a sign-in form.
Exits: r13-ui 1, r13-ui-withdrawn 1 (both attempts; it timed out looking for a sign-in form that never appears), r13-session-end-ui 1 (EN/AR in-app-link FAIL, reload controls PASS), default-limits 1 (EN FAIL, then the next context timed out because of the lock-out).
The cause is in the web client and dates from DG1 (4cd9224): LoginPage's `if (me.data) Navigate(returnTo)` uses the stale cached /me, and RequireSession sends the user back to /login. D-073 did not change the web.

summary:
FAIL, because of one new High finding: F-DG2-480 (web client; pre-existing since DG1; exposed by the D-073 repairs). On source fidelity and operating logic the candidate is faithful: all 26 assigned requirements verify against the playbook, live and in EN/AR.
- Source texts: B0009, B0018 (role names singular), B0023, B0029, B0035 (14 fields), B0037, B0039-43, B0056 and B0062 match the source.
- Gates: G1 -> G2 -> G3 are sequential and were decided live on synthetic data.
- Charter and direction: one current North Star; the 3-5 top-outcome warning and the good-outcome test work; G2 is blocked at zero guardrails.
- Invariants: unquantified pools are labelled; decimals are used; the brand is provisional; there is no certification claim; DG0-DG7 are untouched.
The D-073 server behaviour is correct:
- uploads in EN and AR are byte-identical;
- access ending mid-stream gives 403 (audited), and revocation or sign-out gives 401, with nothing stored and no .part left;
- SIGTERM during an upload exits 0 with no partial file, and evidence works after a restart;
- dev sign-in works for every seeded user and in the browser in EN/AR.
However, the real user outcome of a refused upload, and of any session that ends while the app is open, is broken. The client loops between /login and the page on a blank screen, with no form and no localized message, at about 130-140 /me requests per second. With default rate limits it exhausts the per-IP bucket and shows a stale signed-in shell with 'Too many requests'. Only a manual reload recovers.
